sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: Sentence एक complete thought express करती है — subject (कौन/क्या) और predicate (क्या होता है) दोनों होना ज़रूरी है।
sections.examples:
Example:
The cat sleeps on the mat.
Subject: The cat | Predicate: sleeps on the mat

Children play in the park every evening.

Key rules याद रखो:
- हर sentence capital letter से start होती है।
- Statement period (.) से end होती है।
- सिर्फ words का group भी sentence नहीं — complete idea चाहिए।

Fragment check: "Running in the morning." — यह sentence नहीं, क्योंकि subject missing है।

sections.title: Subject and Predicate
sections.body: Subject बताता है sentence किस बारे में है; predicate बताता है subject क्या करता है या कैसा है।
sections.examples:
Example:
Subject: The teacher | Predicate: explained the lesson clearly.

Subject: Rain | Predicate: fell heavily last night.

Fragment (sentence नहीं): Running in the morning.

Rules:
- Subject usually noun या pronoun होता है।
- Predicate में हमेशा एक verb होता है।
- Fragment में subject या complete predicate missing होता है।

Tip: Verb से पहले "कौन?" या "क्या?" पूछो — जो मिले वही subject है।

sections.title: Sentence Types
sections.body: End punctuation से पता चलता है sentence statement, question, command, या exclamation है।
sections.examples:
Example:
She reads every evening. (statement — period)
Do you read often? (question — ?)
Close the door, please. (command — often no subject "you")
What a beautiful sunset! (exclamation — !)

Rules:
- Questions हमेशा ? से end होते हैं।
- Commands में अक्सर "you" छुपा होता है: (You) sit down.
- Exclamations strong emotion दिखाते हैं — formal writing में कम use करो।

sections.title: Simple and Compound Sentences
sections.body: Simple sentence में एक independent clause होता है; compound में दो या ज़्यादा clauses and, but, or, so से जुड़ते हैं।
sections.examples:
Example:
Simple: Birds sing in the morning.
Compound: Birds sing, and the sun rises.
Compound: I wanted to go, but it started raining.

Rules:
- दो full sentences जोड़ते वक्त and/but/or से पहले comma लगाओ।
- दोनों clauses compound sentence में independent होने चाहिए।
- सिर्फ comma से दो sentences मत जोड़ो — यह comma splice है।

sections.title: Complex Sentences
sections.body: Complex sentence में एक independent clause और कम से कम एक dependent clause होता है — because, when, if, although से start हो सकता है।
sections.examples:
Example:
I stayed home because it was raining.
Although she was tired, she finished her homework.
When the bell rang, the students left.

Rules:
- Dependent clause अकेला sentence नहीं बन सकता।
- जब dependent clause पहले आए, comma लगाओ: Although she was tired, she finished...
- Independent clause अकेला भी चल सकता है; dependent नहीं।

sections.title: Common Sentence Errors
sections.body: Run-on और fragment सबसे common errors हैं — सही punctuation और complete subject-predicate से fix होते हैं।
sections.examples:
Example:
Run-on: I woke up late I missed the bus.
Fixed: I woke up late, so I missed the bus.

Fragment: Because it was cold.
Fixed: Because it was cold, we stayed indoors.

Rules:
- Comma splice: सिर्फ comma से दो sentences मत जोड़ो।
- ज़ोर से पढ़कर run-on और fragment पकड़ो।
- हर sentence में कम से कम एक subject और एक finite verb होना चाहिए।

sections.title: Active and Passive Voice
sections.body: Active voice में subject action करता है; passive में subject action receive करता है — formal writing में passive ज़्यादा use होता है।
sections.examples:
Example:
Active: The chef cooked the meal.
Passive: The meal was cooked by the chef.

Active: Students submitted the assignments.
Passive: The assignments were submitted by the students.

Rules:
- Passive: be + past participle (is written, was built, has been done).
- By-agent optional: The window was broken. (कौन तोड़ा — unknown)
- Active ज़्यादा direct और clear — prefer active जब तक passive better fit न हो।

sections.title: Sentence Combining Practice
sections.body: Chhote sentences को and, but, because, although, when से जोड़कर fluent paragraph बनाओ — variety reader को engage रखती है।
sections.examples:
Example:
Simple pair: I finished my homework. I watched a movie.
Combined: After I finished my homework, I watched a movie.

Three shorts: The rain stopped. We went outside. We played cricket.
Combined: When the rain stopped, we went outside and played cricket.

Drill:
1. She was tired. She continued working. → Although she was tired, she continued working.
2. He studied hard. He passed the exam. → He studied hard, so he passed the exam.

Rules:
- एक paragraph में simple, compound, complex mix करो।
- Same idea repeat मत करो — combine या rephrase करो।

sections.title: Paragraph Coherence
sections.body: अच्छा paragraph connected sentences का group है — topic sentence, supporting details, और closing line से flow clear रहता है।
sections.examples:
Sample paragraph:
Topic: Morning routines help productivity.
Supporting: Waking early gives quiet time. A healthy breakfast fuels focus. Planning the day reduces stress.
Closing: Small habits create a strong start.

Coherence checks:
- हर sentence same main idea support करे?
- Transition words smooth हैं? (First, Then, However, Finally)
- Pronouns clear refer करें (he/she/they = कौन?)

Rules:
- Topic sentence पहले या second line में main point दे।
- One paragraph = one main idea.
- Last sentence summary या gentle conclusion दे।

sections.title: Sentence Self-Test
sections.body: नीचे tasks solve करो — answers mentally check करो, फिर aloud पढ़कर natural flow verify करो।
sections.examples:
Task 1 — Identify type:
a) Where is the library? → interrogative
b) Please sit down. → command
c) What a surprise! → exclamation

Task 2 — Fix the error:
Wrong: Although he was late. He entered quietly.
Correct: Although he was late, he entered quietly.

Task 3 — Combine:
The team won. The fans cheered loudly.
→ The team won, and the fans cheered loudly.

Task 4 — Active to passive:
They built a new bridge. → A new bridge was built by them.

Tip: Daily 5 sentences लिखो — subject, verb, correct end mark check करो।

resources.title: BBC Learning English — Sentence Structure Basics
British Council — English Grammar Reference: Sentence Structure
Purdue OWL — Sentence Structure and Types

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: Tense बताता है action past, present, या future में कब होता है — consistent tense से reader confuse नहीं होता।
sections.examples:
Example:
Present: She walks to school.
Past: She walked to school.
Future: She will walk to school.

English में 12 main tense forms हैं, लेकिन तीन time frames base हैं: past, present, future.

Rules:
- एक paragraph में tense match रखो जब तक time clearly change न हो।
- Time words (yesterday, tomorrow, now) tense choose करने में help करते हैं।

sections.title: Simple Present
sections.body: Habits, routines, general truths, और fixed schedules के लिए simple present use होता है।
sections.examples:
Example:
Habit: He plays tennis on Sundays.
Truth: Water boils at 100°C.
Question: Do they live nearby?
Negative: She does not like spicy food.

Rules:
- he/she/it के साथ affirmative में verb + s/es: He plays, She watches.
- Questions और negatives में do/does: Does she know? / She does not know.
- Stative verbs (know, like, believe) अक्सर simple present में ही रहते हैं।

sections.title: Present Continuous
sections.body: अभी हो रही action, temporary situation, या planned near-future के लिए am/is/are + verb-ing use करो।
sections.examples:
Example:
Now: She is reading a book.
Temporary: I am staying with my aunt this week.
Planned: We are meeting them tomorrow.

Rules:
- Moment of speaking पर चल रही action के लिए use करो।
- Stative verbs (know, want, belong) में usually -ing मत लगाओ।
- Always, usually, every day के साथ simple present better है, continuous नहीं।

sections.title: Simple Past
sections.body: Past में किसी specific time पर complete हुई action के लिए — regular verbs +ed, irregular अलग form।
sections.examples:
Example:
Regular: They visited London last year.
Irregular: She went home early. (go → went)
Time marker: Yesterday, I finished my project.

Common irregular: see→saw, eat→ate, take→took, come→came

Rules:
- yesterday, last week, ago simple past signal करते हैं।
- Past में did use करो — main verb base form में: Did she go? (not Did she went?)
- Irregular past forms याद करना important है।

sections.title: Simple Future
sections.body: Future के लिए will + base verb या am/is/are + going to + base verb — will spontaneous, going to planned।
sections.examples:
Example:
Will (decision/promise): I will help you with homework.
Going to (plan/evidence): It is going to rain — look at those clouds.
Future time: Next month, we will start a new course.

Rules:
- Timetable/schedule के लिए will नहीं — simple present: The train leaves at 6.
- going to = पहले से plan या visible evidence.
- will = अभी decide किया या promise।

sections.title: Perfect Tenses Overview
sections.body: Perfect tenses दो time points connect करते हैं — present perfect past को अब तक link करता है।
sections.examples:
Example:
Present perfect: I have lived here for five years.
Past perfect: When I arrived, the movie had already started.
Experience: She has visited three countries.

Rules:
- Present perfect: have/has + past participle — result या duration अब तक।
- Past perfect: had + past participle — दो past events में पहले वाली।
- for/since present perfect के साथ common: for 5 years, since 2020.

sections.title: Past Continuous
sections.body: Past में किसी specific moment पर ongoing action — was/were + verb-ing; often simple past के साथ background action।
sections.examples:
Example:
At 8 p.m., I was studying for the exam.
While she was cooking, the phone rang.
They were playing when it started raining.

Rules:
- was + I/he/she/it | were + you/we/they
- When + simple past, past continuous: When I arrived, they were waiting.
- Stative verbs (know, believe) में usually continuous नहीं।

sections.title: Present Perfect vs Simple Past
sections.body: Simple past = finished time (yesterday, last week); present perfect = connection to now, no exact finished time।
sections.examples:
Example:
Simple past: I saw that movie yesterday.
Present perfect: I have seen that movie. (experience — when unclear)

Wrong: I have finished it yesterday. | Correct: I finished it yesterday.

Correct present perfect: I have just eaten. | I have never been to Japan.

Rules:
- yesterday, ago, last year → simple past only.
- just, already, yet, ever, never → often present perfect.
- Indian English में sometimes mix — exam में strict rule follow करो।

sections.title: Future Forms in Detail
sections.body: Will, going to, present continuous (future), और simple present (timetable) — context decide करता है कौन सा future form।
sections.examples:
Example:
Spontaneous: I'll answer the door.
Plan: We're going to visit Delhi next month.
Arrangement: I'm meeting Ravi at six. (fixed plan)
Timetable: The train leaves at 9:15. (schedule)

Rules:
- going to + evidence: Look — it's going to rain.
- will + promise/offer/decision at moment of speaking.
- Present continuous future = personal arrangement with time/place.

sections.title: Tense Consistency
sections.body: एक paragraph या story में tense jump मत करो जब तक time shift clearly signal न हो — reader confuse हो जाता है।
sections.examples:
Example (inconsistent):
Wrong: Yesterday I go to market and bought vegetables.
Correct: Yesterday I went to the market and bought vegetables.

Narrative tip:
Past story → mostly simple past; flashback → past perfect.

Rules:
- Reported speech में tense often shift: He said he was tired.
- Historical facts → simple present OK: The sun rises in the east.
- Headlines sometimes present tense: Prime Minister visits city.

sections.title: Tense Error Correction Drill
sections.body: नीचे common Hindi-English tense mistakes fix करो — daily 10 sentences practice से habit बनती है।
sections.examples:
Fix these:
1. I am knowing him since 2020. → I have known him since 2020.
2. She did not went home. → She did not go home.
3. He will goes tomorrow. → He will go tomorrow.
4. When I was child, I have played cricket. → When I was a child, I played cricket.
5. I am living here since five years. → I have lived here for five years.

Quick reference:
for + duration | since + starting point
 did + base verb | has/has + past participle

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: Noun person, place, thing, या idea का नाम बताता है — sentence में अक्सर subject या object होता है।
sections.examples:
Example:
Person: teacher | Place: Delhi | Thing: book | Idea: freedom

The teacher opened the book in Delhi.

Noun से "कौन?" या "क्या?" का जवाब मिलता है।

Singular/plural, countable/uncountable — ये सब noun की properties हैं जो आगे detail में cover करेंगे।

sections.title: Types of Noun
sections.body: Noun को मुख्यतः पाँच types में बाँटा जाता है — हर type का sentence में अलग role होता है।
sections.examples:
Noun को मुख्यतः पाँच types में बाँटा जाता है:
1. Proper Noun — किसी specific person, place, या thing का नाम। हमेशा capital letter से शुरू होता है। Example: Sumit, India, Taj Mahal, Monday.
2. Common Noun — general नाम, किसी particular चीज़ का नहीं। Example: boy, city, monument, day.
देखो difference — "India" proper noun है (specific country), लेकिन "country" common noun है (कोई भी country हो सकता है)।
3. Collective Noun — एक group of things या people को represent करता है। Example: team, family, class, herd.
जैसे "A team of players" — यहाँ "team" एक collective noun है क्योंकि वो कई players को एक साथ represent कर रहा है।
4. Material Noun — किसी material या substance का नाम, जिससे चीज़ें बनती हैं। Example: gold, wood, water, cotton.
5. Abstract Noun — वो चीज़ें जो हम touch या देख नहीं सकते, सिर्फ feel कर सकते हैं — qualities, feelings, ideas। Example: honesty, happiness, courage, love.

Example sentences:
Sumit (Proper) joined the team (Collective) in Delhi (Proper).
Honesty (Abstract) is more valuable than gold (Material).

sections.title: Countable and Uncountable Nouns
sections.body: Countable nouns गिन सकते हो (one apple, two apples); uncountable को quantity से measure करते हो (some water, much rice)।
sections.examples:
Example:
Countable — Singular: one apple, a chair | Plural: three apples, many chairs
Uncountable: water, milk, sugar, homework, advice, information

Wrong: two advices | Correct: two pieces of advice
Wrong: many furnitures | Correct: much furniture

Rules:
- Singular countable के साथ a/an use करो।
- Plural countable के साथ a/an नहीं।
- Uncountable के साथ some/any/much; plural form मत बनाओ (no waters, no advices)।

sections.title: Singular and Plural Forms
sections.body: ज़्यादा तर nouns -s/-es से plural बनते हैं; कुछ irregular हैं और कुछ दोनों form में same रहते हैं।
sections.examples:
Example:
Regular: cat→cats, box→boxes, city→cities
Irregular: child→children, man→men, foot→feet, mouse→mice
Same both forms: one sheep, two sheep | one fish, two fish

Rules:
- -y ending: consonant + y → -ies (city→cities); vowel + y → -s (boy→boys).
- -f/-fe ending अक्सर -ves: knife→knives, leaf→leaves.
- Uncountable nouns का plural नहीं होता — dictionary check करो अगर doubt हो।

sections.title: Nouns in Sentences
sections.body: Noun subject, direct object, indirect object, या preposition के बाद object बन सकता है।
sections.examples:
Example:
Subject: The dog barked.
Direct object: She bought flowers.
Indirect object: He gave his sister a gift.
After preposition: We talked about the exam.

Tip:
- Verb से पहले कौन/क्या → subject noun.
- Transitive verb के बाद क्या → object noun.
- Preposition के तुरंत बाद noun या pronoun आता है।

sections.title: Common Noun Errors
sections.body: Hindi speakers अक्सर uncountable nouns को plural बनाते हैं या proper noun capitalize करना भूल जाते हैं।
sections.examples:
Example:
Wrong: I need informations. | Correct: I need information.
Wrong: she lives in mumbai. | Correct: She lives in Mumbai.
Wrong: The team are playing well. (US: team = singular) | Correct: The team is playing well.

Rules:
- Proper nouns हमेशा capital — cities, names, brands, days, months.
- advice, furniture, luggage, news — uncountable, plural मत बनाओ।
- Collective noun singular या plural हो सकता है — meaning के हिसाब से decide करो।

sections.title: Gerunds and Infinitives as Nouns
sections.body: Gerund (-ing form as noun) और infinitive (to + verb) sentence में noun की तरह काम करते हैं — verb choose करने से meaning change हो सकती है।
sections.examples:
Example:
Gerund as subject: Swimming is good exercise.
Gerund after preposition: She is good at dancing.
Infinitive as subject: To learn English takes time.

Like vs love + gerund/infinitive:
I like reading. | I want to read.

Rules:
- enjoy, avoid, finish, mind → usually gerund after: He finished writing.
- want, decide, hope, plan → usually infinitive: She decided to leave.
- Some verbs both: start reading / start to read.

sections.title: Noun Clauses
sections.body: Noun clause whole sentence में noun की job करता है — that, what, whether, who introduce कर सकते हैं।
sections.examples:
Example:
Subject: What she said surprised everyone.
Object: I know that he is honest.
After preposition: We talked about whether the plan would work.

Compare:
Noun: honesty | Noun phrase: her honesty | Noun clause: that she was honest

Rules:
- that-clause often object: She believes that he will come.
- Question word clauses: I don't know where he lives.
- whether/if: Tell me whether you agree.

sections.title: Quantifiers with Nouns
sections.body: Some, any, many, much, few, little, a lot of — countable vs uncountable के साथ correct quantifier choose करो।
sections.examples:
Example:
Countable: many books, a few friends, several options
Uncountable: much water, a little time, some advice
Both: a lot of people, a lot of money

Wrong: much students | Correct: many students
Wrong: few water | Correct: little water

Rules:
- some = affirmative | any = questions/negatives (usually)
- a few = some (positive) | few = almost none
- a little = some amount | little = almost none

sections.title: Noun Identification Drills
sections.body: हर sentence में nouns underline करो — type (proper/common/collective/material/abstract) label करो।
sections.examples:
Drill 1:
The team celebrated victory with joy in Mumbai.
team (collective), victory (abstract), joy (abstract), Mumbai (proper)

Drill 2 — Fix errors:
Wrong: She gave me many informations.
Correct: She gave me a lot of information.

Drill 3 — Plural:
child → children | tooth → teeth | phenomenon → phenomena

Drill 4 — Countable or not?
news (uncountable) | chair (countable) | homework (uncountable)

resources.title: British Council — English Grammar Reference: Nouns
Grammarly — A Complete Guide to Nouns

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: Pronoun noun की जगह लेता है ताकि repetition न हो — antecedent (जिस noun की जगह ले) से number और person match करना ज़रूरी है।
sections.examples:
Example:
Without pronoun: Ravi met Ravi's friend.
With pronoun: Ravi met his friend.

She is a doctor. They work at the hospital.

Rules:
- Pronoun का reference clear होना चाहिए — reader को पता हो "she" कौन है।
- Hindi में gender ज़्यादा flexible है; English में he/she/they carefully choose करो।

sections.title: Personal Pronouns
sections.body: Subject forms verb से पहले; object forms verb या preposition के बाद आते हैं।
sections.examples:
Example:
Subject: I, you, he, she, it, we, they
Object: me, you, him, her, it, us, them

She sings well. (subject)
The teacher called him. (object)
We invited them to dinner.

Rules:
- दो subjects के बीच "I" last आता है: You and I are friends. (not I and you)
- After preposition object form: between you and me (not I).
- it = things/animals; they plural के लिए people या things दोनों।

sections.title: Possessive Pronouns
sections.body: Possessive adjectives noun से पहले (my book); possessive pronouns अकेले stand करते हैं (The book is mine)।
sections.examples:
Example:
Adjective + noun: This is her book. | Their house is big.
Pronoun alone: This book is hers. | That house is theirs.

its (possessive) vs it's (it is) — बहुत common mistake!

Rules:
- hers, theirs, ours में apostrophe नहीं।
- its = belonging to it | it's = it is या it has.
- my/mine, your/yours — adjective noun के साथ, pronoun अकेला।

sections.title: Demonstrative Pronouns
sections.body: this/these (near) और that/those (far) — singular/plural match करो।
sections.examples:
Example:
Near: This is my pen. These are my notes.
Far: That was a great movie. Those were expensive shoes.

As adjective: This book is interesting. (this + noun)

Rules:
- this/that = singular | these/those = plural.
- Distance physical हो सकती है या conversation/time में (that day, this week).
- Those who work hard succeed. (those = people — relative sense)

sections.title: Reflexive and Relative Pronouns
sections.body: Reflexive subject को वापस point करते हैं; relative noun describe करने वाले clause introduce करते हैं।
sections.examples:
Example:
Reflexive: She taught herself to cook. | They enjoyed themselves.
Relative: The woman who called is my aunt.
The book that I borrowed is due tomorrow.

who = people | which = things | that = both (restrictive clauses)

Rules:
- myself, yourself — subject के साथ match: I did it myself.
- who vs whom: whom object position में (formal).
- Don't use myself instead of me: Ravi and I went. (not Ravi and myself)

sections.title: Pronoun Agreement
sections.body: Pronoun antecedent के number और gender से match करे — vague reference से reader confuse होता है।
sections.examples:
Example:
Correct: Each student must bring their ID. (modern inclusive)
Correct: The students finished their projects.

Vague: When Priya met Ananya, she was happy. — कौन happy थी?
Clear: Priya was happy when she met Ananya.

Rules:
- Plural antecedent → plural pronoun: The dogs wagged their tails.
- Everyone, someone → singular they/their acceptable in modern English.
- Antecedent sentence में पहले आए, फिर pronoun।

resources.title: British Council — English Grammar Reference: Pronouns

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: Verb action, event, या state of being express करता है — हर complete sentence में कम से कम एक verb होना चाहिए।
sections.examples:
Example:
Action: The children run in the park.
State: She feels tired.

Verbs tense और subject के हिसाब से form change करते हैं: run / runs / ran / running.

Rules:
- Predicate का heart verb है।
- Base form, past, past participle याद करो — irregular list important है।

sections.title: Action Verbs
sections.body: Physical या mental activity दिखाते हैं — run, write, think, build, learn।
sections.examples:
Example:
Physical: He kicks the ball.
Mental: She understands the lesson.
Ongoing: They are building a new school.

Test: "What did X do?" से action verb identify होता है।

Rules:
- बहुत से action verbs transitive हैं — direct object ले सकते हैं।
- Mental verbs भी action category में आते हैं English grammar में।

sections.title: Linking Verbs
sections.body: Subject को description या rename से connect करते हैं — be, seem, become, feel, look, sound, taste, smell।
sections.examples:
Example:
Be: She is a nurse.
Seem: The problem seems difficult.
Sensory: The soup smells delicious.

Rules:
- Linking verb के बाद adjective आता है, adverb नहीं: She looks happy. (not happily)
- Linking verb action नहीं दिखाता — state या condition.
- become, grow, turn भी linking हो सकते हैं: The sky turned dark.

sections.title: Subject-Verb Agreement
sections.body: Singular subject → singular verb; plural subject → plural verb — बीच के words confuse मत करो।
sections.examples:
Example:
Singular: The dog runs fast.
Plural: The dogs run fast.
Tricky: The list of items is on the desk. (subject = list, not items)

Rules:
- he/she/it + simple present verb + s: She runs, It works.
- Prepositional phrase ignore करके subject ढूँढो: One of the students is absent.
- Neither...nor → verb second subject के साथ match: Neither he nor they are ready.

sections.title: Helping Verbs
sections.body: Auxiliary verbs (be, have, do, will, can, must) main verb के साथ tenses, questions, negatives बनाते हैं।
sections.examples:
Example:
Perfect: She has finished her work.
Question: Do you understand?
Modal: You must wear a helmet.
Future: They will arrive soon.

Rules:
- Modals (can, must, should) के बाद base verb — no to: She can swim. (not can to swim)
- do/does/did simple tenses के questions/negatives में।
- has/have/had + past participle perfect tenses के लिए।

sections.title: Transitive and Intransitive Verbs
sections.body: Transitive verb direct object लेता है; intransitive नहीं — कुछ verbs दोनों तरह use होते हैं।
sections.examples:
Example:
Transitive: He wrote a letter. (letter = object)
Intransitive: The baby cried. (no object needed)
Both: She eats. / She eats rice.

Rules:
- Verb के बाद "what?" या "whom?" → transitive with object.
- No object possible → intransitive: sleep, arrive, happen.
- Agreement rules सब verb types पर same apply होते हैं।

resources.title: British Council — English Grammar Reference: Verbs

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: Adjective noun या pronoun को describe या modify करता है — size, color, age, opinion, material वगैरह बताता है।
sections.examples:
Example:
The red car is fast.
She has a beautiful voice.

Adjectives answer: What kind? Which one? How many?

Rules:
- English में adjective usually noun से पहले आता है (unlike Hindi post-position)।
- Multiple adjectives एक natural order follow करते हैं।

sections.title: Descriptive Adjectives
sections.body: Qualities add करते हैं — tall, happy, cold, intelligent, wooden — reader को picture clear होती है।
sections.examples:
Example:
The old house stood on a quiet street.
He gave an honest answer.
Three happy children played outside.

Rules:
- Opinion adjectives (lovely, nice) size से पहले: a lovely big garden.
- Number adjectives order में पहले या बाद में specific position: three large boxes.
- Proper adjectives capital: Indian food, French wine.

sections.title: Comparative and Superlative
sections.body: दो चीज़ों की तुलना comparative (-er / more); तीन या ज़्यादा की superlative (-est / most)।
sections.examples:
Example:
Comparative: This book is longer than that one.
Superlative: She is the smartest student in class.

Irregular: good→better→best | bad→worse→worst | far→farther/further→furthest

Rules:
- Short adjectives: -er/-est (tall, taller, tallest).
- Long adjectives: more/most (interesting, more interesting, most interesting).
- than comparative के बाद; the superlative से पहले।

sections.title: Adjective Order
sections.body: कई adjectives एक साथ आए तो order: opinion → size → age → shape → color → origin → material → purpose + noun।
sections.examples:
Example:
A beautiful small old round red Italian wooden dining table.

Natural: a lovely big house
Unnatural: a red big house (size usually color से पहले)

Rules:
- सब adjectives को "and" से noun से पहले मत जोड़ो।
- General rule याद करो — native speakers भी intuition से करते हैं।
- दो adjectives enough हैं ज़्यादा तर sentences के लिए।

sections.title: Predicate Adjectives
sections.body: Linking verb के बाद subject describe करते हैं — noun से पहले नहीं आते।
sections.examples:
Example:
The food tastes spicy.
He seems confident.
The children grew tired after the game.

Wrong: She feels happily. | Correct: She feels happy.

Rules:
- Linking verb + adjective (not adverb for description of subject).
- taste, smell, look, feel, sound — sensory linking verbs.
- Predicate adjective subject को modify करता है, verb को नहीं।

sections.title: Common Adjective Errors
sections.body: Double comparative, adjective/adverb confusion, और -ed/-ing adjective mix-up common mistakes हैं।
sections.examples:
Example:
Wrong: more better | Correct: better
Wrong: He speaks English good. | Correct: He speaks English well. (adverb modifies verb)

I am bored (मैं feel कर रहा) vs The movie is boring (movie cause करती है)।

Rules:
- -ed = person की feeling | -ing = cause of feeling.
- Adjectives modify nouns; adverbs modify verbs, adjectives, other adverbs.
- very + adjective OK; very + adverb भी: very quickly.

resources.title: British Council — English Grammar Reference: Adjectives
Purdue OWL — Adjectives and Adjective Clauses

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: Punctuation meaning clear करती है, ideas अलग करती है, और pauses दिखाती है — गलत comma पूरा meaning बदल सकता है।
sections.examples:
Example:
Let's eat, Grandma! (Grandma को बुला रहे हो)
Let's eat Grandma! (completely different — dangerous meaning!)

Main marks: . ? ! , ' " : ; —

Rules:
- Punctuation reader की speed और understanding guide करती है।
- Formal writing में consistent style follow करो (US vs UK थोड़े rules different)।

sections.title: Periods, Question Marks, and Exclamation Marks
sections.body: Statements period से; direct questions ? से; strong emotion ! से — formal में exclamation कम use करो।
sections.examples:
Example:
Statement: The meeting starts at nine.
Question: Are you coming to the meeting?
Exclamation: What a great idea!

Indirect question (no ?): She asked whether I was coming.

Rules:
- Formal text में multiple !!! avoid करो।
- Every statement end mark चाहिए।
- Question word order change होता है indirect में।

sections.title: Commas
sections.body: Lists, clauses, introductory phrases, और extra information के लिए — comma splice से बचो।
sections.examples:
Example:
List: We bought apples, oranges, and grapes.
Intro: After the exam, we celebrated.
Non-essential: My brother, who lives in Pune, is visiting.

Comma splice (wrong): I was tired, I went to bed.
Fixed: I was tired, so I went to bed. OR I was tired. I went to bed.

Rules:
- Oxford comma (and से पहले) optional पर lists clear करती है।
- Dependent clause पहले → comma: When I arrived, she left.
- Essential info में comma नहीं: The student who studied passed.

sections.title: Apostrophes
sections.body: Possession (Sarah's bag) और contractions (don't = do not) — simple plurals के लिए apostrophe नहीं।
sections.examples:
Example:
Singular possessive: Sarah's bag
Plural possessive: the students' books (s के बाद ')
Contraction: it's = it is | its = possessive

Wrong: two cat's | Correct: two cats

Rules:
- its vs it's — top mistake for learners.
- Plural ending in s: add ' after s (teachers' room).
- Decades: 1990s (no apostrophe for plural years).

sections.title: Quotation Marks and Colons
sections.body: Direct speech और short work titles quotes में; colon lists या explanation introduce करता है।
sections.examples:
Example:
Speech: She said, "I will be late."
Colon list: Bring three items: a pen, paper, and ID.
Explanation: He had one goal: to finish the marathon.

Rules:
- US English: periods और commas quotes के अंदर।
- Colon से पहले complete sentence होना चाहिए।
- Wrong: The ingredients include: flour and sugar. (verb के बाद directly colon नहीं)

sections.title: Semicolons and Dashes
sections.body: Semicolon related independent clauses जोड़ता है; dash emphasis या extra info के लिए comma से ज़्यादा strong।
sections.examples:
Example:
Semicolon: The storm passed; the sun came out.
Dash: Three skills — reading, writing, and speaking — are essential.
Complex list: I visited Delhi, India; Paris, France; and Tokyo, Japan.

Rules:
- Semicolon जब clauses related हों पर अलग भी चल सकें।
- Formal essays में dash overuse मत करो।
- Semicolon list items में जब items के अंदर comma हो।

resources.title: BBC Learning English — Punctuation in Writing

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: तीन articles: a, an, the — noun से पहले आते हैं; Hindi में direct equivalent नहीं, इसलिए यह common challenge है।
sections.examples:
Example:
Indefinite: I saw a dog in the park. (कोई भी dog)
Definite: The dog was friendly. (वही specific dog)

An apple a day keeps the doctor away.

Rules:
- a/an = indefinite, non-specific.
- the = definite, specific या already known.
- Articles सिर्फ singular countable के साथ a/an; the सब types के साथ।

sections.title: A vs An
sections.body: Consonant sound से पहले a, vowel sound से पहले an — spelling नहीं, pronunciation matter करती है।
sections.examples:
Example:
a book, a university (yoo- sound = consonant)
an hour (silent h), an umbrella, an honest person

Wrong: a apple | Correct: an apple

Rules:
- an hour, an MBA (M sounds like em = vowel sound).
- a European, a one-way street (consonant sound).
- Acronyms: pronunciation से decide — an FBI agent (eff = vowel sound).

sections.title: When to Use The
sections.body: जब reader को पता हो कौनसी चीज़, unique चीज़, या पहले mention हुई चीज़ हो।
sections.examples:
Example:
Specific: Please close the door. (वो door)
Unique: the sun, the moon, the president (context में)
Second mention: I bought a phone. The phone is new.

Rules:
- Superlative के साथ: the best student.
- General plural without the: Dogs are loyal.
- Musical instruments: She plays the piano.

sections.title: When Not to Use Articles
sections.body: Plural या uncountable general statements, proper nouns, languages, meals, और institutions के लिए often no article।
sections.examples:
Example:
Language: She speaks Hindi. (no article)
General: Life is beautiful.
Specific life: The life of a soldier is hard.

Wrong: I need an advice. | Correct: I need some advice.

Rules:
- People/cities usually no the: Ravi, Mumbai (not the Mumbai).
- Meals: have breakfast, eat lunch (no article).
- by + transport: by bus, by train (no the).

sections.title: Articles with Jobs and Nationalities
sections.body: Singular countable job title के साथ a/an ज़रूरी; nationality adjective usually no article।
sections.examples:
Example:
Job: He is a doctor. | She is an engineer.
Nationality: She is Indian. (adjective, no article)

Wrong: She is teacher. | Correct: She is a teacher.
Plural jobs: They are teachers. (no article)

Rules:
- a/an singular countable profession के लिए।
- the + nationality noun = people group: the French, the Japanese.
- Generic: A teacher needs patience. (any teacher)

sections.title: Common Article Errors
sections.body: Articles जहाँ चाहिए वहाँ छोड़ देना या जहाँ नहीं चाहिए वहाँ लगाना — fixed phrases याद करो।
sections.examples:
Example:
Wrong: She goes to the school every day. (institution)
Correct: She goes to school.

Wrong: I am good in English.
Correct: I am good at English. (preposition, not article — but related!)

Fixed phrases: at home, in bed, in prison, by car

Rules:
- some advice, some information — uncountable, no a.
- the + adjective = group: the rich, the poor.
- Names of most countries no the: India, France (exceptions: the UK, the USA).

resources.title: British Council — English Grammar Reference: Articles

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body: Prepositions time, place, direction, या manner का relation दिखाते हैं — noun/pronoun को sentence से connect करते हैं।
sections.examples:
Example:
Place: The book is on the table.
Time: We meet at noon.
Direction: She walked to the store.

Common: in, on, at, by, with, for, to, from, about, between, among

Rules:
- Preposition के बाद noun या pronoun (object of preposition).
- Hindi से direct translate मत करो — collocation याद करो।

sections.title: In, On, At — Place
sections.body: In = enclosed/large area; on = surface; at = specific point या address।
sections.examples:
Example:
in: the room, India, the car, the box
on: the wall, the floor, Main Street, page 5
at: the door, the station, 42 Oak Lane, home

Rules:
- in the corner (room) vs on the corner (street intersection).
- at home / in the house — दोनों चल सकते हैं context से।
- on TV, on the internet, on a bus (British also in a bus).

sections.title: In, On, At — Time
sections.body: In = longer periods; on = days/dates; at = clock time और specific moments।
sections.examples:
Example:
in: March, 2024, the morning, the 1990s
on: Monday, 15 August, my birthday, Christmas Day
at: 5 p.m., night, the moment, noon

Rules:
- in the morning BUT at night (fixed phrases).
- on weekend (US) vs at the weekend (UK).
- on time = punctual | in time = before deadline.

sections.title: Common Preposition Pairs
sections.body: Verbs और adjectives specific prepositions माँगते हैं — units की तरह याद करो।
sections.examples:
Example:
depend on, listen to, arrive at/in, agree with, afraid of, interested in
married to, good at, famous for, different from/than

Wrong: depend from | Correct: depend on
Wrong: listen music | Correct: listen to music

Rules:
- arrive at small place (station), arrive in city/country (Delhi, India).
- discuss something (no preposition) — NOT discuss about.
- explain something to someone (not explain someone).

sections.title: Prepositions of Movement
sections.body: To = toward; from = origin; into/onto/through/across/along path और direction बताते हैं।
sections.examples:
Example:
to school, from Delhi to Mumbai
into the room (movement inside), in the room (static)
through the tunnel, across the bridge, along the river

Rules:
- go to destination (not go in school for daily attendance).
- into = movement; in = position.
- onto = movement to surface; on = on surface already.

sections.title: Phrasal Verbs and Common Errors
sections.body: Verb + preposition/particle (give up, look after) — meaning अलग words से अलग हो सकती है।
sections.examples:
Example:
give up = quit | look after = take care of | turn on = activate
put off = postpone | run out of = finish supply

Wrong: I am good in English. | Correct: I am good at English.
Wrong: discuss about | Correct: discuss

Rules:
- Phrasal verbs spoken English में बहुत common.
- Separable phrasal verbs: turn off the light / turn the light off.
- Inseparable: look after the baby (not look the baby after).

resources.title: Purdue OWL — Prepositions and Prepositional Phrases

sections.title: Review Checklist
sections.body: सारे core topics एक बार revise करो — जो confidently explain कर सको, tick करो।
sections.examples:
Checklist:
1. Subject और predicate identify कर सकता हूँ?
2. Verb tenses consistently use करता हूँ?
3. Nouns को 5 types में classify कर सकता हूँ (Proper, Common, Collective, Material, Abstract)?
4. Pronouns antecedent से match करते हैं?
5. Subject-verb agreement सही है?
6. Adjective order और comparative/superlative सही?
7. Commas, apostrophes, end marks correct?
8. a/an/the सही जगह?
9. Preposition collocations (good at, depend on) याद हैं?

Tip: एक session में एक topic — depth > speed.

sections.title: Mixed Error Correction
sections.body: हर sentence पढ़ो, error ढूँढो, सही लिखो — कोई भी topic से error हो सकता है।
sections.examples:
Example:
Wrong: She go to school every day.
Correct: She goes to school every day. (subject-verb agreement)

Wrong: Its a sunny day.
Correct: It's a sunny day. (contraction)

Wrong: He is good in mathematics.
Correct: He is good at mathematics. (preposition)

Wrong: I saw a elephant.
Correct: I saw an elephant. (article)

Tip: ज़ोर से पढ़ो — कान से error पहले पकड़ा जाता है।

sections.title: Sentence Building Practice
sections.body: दिए words से correct sentence बनाओ — tense, articles, और word order ध्यान से।
sections.examples:
Example:
Words: she / read / interesting / book / every / night
Answer: She reads an interesting book every night.

Words: they / play / football / in / park / yesterday
Answer: They played football in the park yesterday.

Words: Ravi / and / Priya / finish / their / homework
Answer: Ravi and Priya finished their homework.

Rules:
- Adjectives noun से पहले।
- Countable singular के लिए article check करो।
- Time word से tense decide करो।

sections.title: Tense and Pronoun Drill
sections.body: Sentences को different tense में rewrite करो या nouns को pronouns से replace करो।
sections.examples:
Example:
Present → Past: Ravi eats breakfast at seven. → Ravi ate breakfast at seven.

Noun → Pronoun: Priya finished Priya's homework. → Priya finished her homework.

Past → Future: They visited their grandparents. → They will visit their grandparents.

Rules:
- Pronoun number/gender antecedent से match।
- Time words tense change में help करते हैं।
- Possessive pronoun apostrophe rule याद रखो।

sections.title: Preposition and Article Fill-in
sections.body: Blank में सही preposition या article (a, an, the, या none) choose करो।
sections.examples:
Example:
She arrived ___ the airport at 6 p.m. → at
He needs ___ honest answer. → an
___ water in this bottle is cold. → The
They are interested ___ music. → in
She goes ___ school by bus. → to (no article before school as institution)

Rules:
- at = specific time/place point.
- an = vowel sound; the = known/specific noun.
- by bus, at home — fixed no-article phrases.

sections.title: Extended Writing Challenge
sections.body: अपनी daily routine पर 5–7 sentences लिखो — कम से कम 3 tenses, 2 prepositions, 1 comparative, सही articles।
sections.examples:
Sample:
Every morning I wake up at six. Yesterday I woke up late because my alarm did not ring. I am trying to become an early riser. Breakfast is simpler than dinner. I walk to the bus stop and read a book on the way. Tomorrow I will start a new grammar course.

Self-check after writing:
- हर sentence complete है? (subject + verb)
- Tense consistent within same time frame?
- Proper nouns capitalized?
- Read aloud — natural लगता है?

Rules:
- एक sentence = एक main idea.
- Proofread for articles और prepositions last.

sections.title: Topic-wise Mini Tests
sections.body: Har topic ke baad 5-minute mini test — Sentence, Tense, Noun mix se confidence build hoti hai।
sections.examples:
Mini Test A — Sentence:
1. Identify subject: The children played in the garden.
2. Fix fragment: Because it was raining hard.
3. Combine: She studied. She passed.

Mini Test B — Tense:
1. Present perfect: I ___ (live) here since 2019.
2. Past continuous: They ___ (watch) TV when I called.
3. Fix: He will goes tomorrow.

Mini Test C — Noun:
1. Type of "honesty": abstract
2. Plural of child: children
3. Fix: many furnitures

sections.title: Mixed Error Spotting Set B
sections.body: Har line mein ek ya zyada errors ho sakte hain — type identify karke correct sentence likho।
sections.examples:
1. She don't likes to reading books.
→ She doesn't like to read books.

2. I have went to Delhi last summer.
→ I went to Delhi last summer.

3. The informations on the table are useful.
→ The information on the table is useful.

4. He is good in mathematics since childhood.
→ He has been good at mathematics since childhood.

5. Each of the students have submitted their work.
→ Each of the students has submitted their work.

sections.title: Fill in the Blanks — Mixed Grammar
sections.body: Articles, prepositions, tenses, aur pronouns ek saath practice karo — exam-style blanks।
sections.examples:
1. ___ honest person always speaks ___ truth. → An, the
2. She has been waiting ___ two hours. → for
3. If it ___ tomorrow, we will stay home. → rains
4. Neither Ravi nor his friends ___ ready yet. → are
5. I look forward ___ meeting you. → to
6. This is ___ best movie I have ever seen. → the
7. He gave ___ useful advice. → some (no plural)

sections.title: Paragraph Correction
sections.body: Poorly written paragraph ko revise karo — grammar, punctuation, aur flow improve karo।
sections.examples:
Original:
yesterday i go to market. i buyed many vegetable and return home late because the bus was delay.

Revised:
Yesterday I went to the market. I bought many vegetables and returned home late because the bus was delayed.

Checklist while revising:
- Capitalize sentence start and proper nouns
- Match tense (yesterday → past)
- Irregular past: buy → bought
- Subject-verb: bus was delayed (singular)

sections.title: Weekly Study Plan
sections.body: Consistent short sessions grammar retain karne ke liye best hain — 30 minutes daily recommended।
sections.examples:
Week plan:
Mon — Sentence structure + 10 sentence writing
Tue — Tenses (present + past) + error fixes
Wed — Nouns (types + countability) + drills
Thu — Pronouns + articles
Fri — Verbs + subject-verb agreement
Sat — Workbook mixed exercises
Sun — Review weak topics + read aloud 1 page English

Tip: Notebook mein sirf galat sentences likho — repeat mistakes kam honge.

Progress tracker:
□ I can explain 5 noun types
□ I can fix 8/10 tense errors
□ I write 5 error-free sentences daily

sections.title: Self-Assessment Scorecard
sections.body: Har section ke baad khud ko rate karo 1–5 — 3 se neeche wale topics dubara padho।
sections.examples:
Rate yourself (1 = weak, 5 = strong):
Sentence structure: ___ / 5
Tenses: ___ / 5
Nouns: ___ / 5
Pronouns: ___ / 5
Verbs & agreement: ___ / 5
Articles: ___ / 5
Prepositions: ___ / 5
Punctuation: ___ / 5

Goal: Sab topics par kam se kam 4/5 within 4 weeks.

Action: Lowest score wale topic ka lesson dubara padho, phir Workbook mini test repeat karo.

resources.title: British Council — English Levels and Practice
